answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and drills one basalt core at a summit site, logging length and layer sequence under its own key. A wander auditor re-measures the core; a mismatch or reused core burns the bond. First fee is 26 credits; the kth identity from one funding source pays 26+6(k-1), so the 1,000th pays 6,020 and 1,000 clones pay 3,023,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-core ring fails: a rented core carries its owner's summit stamp and key, so a second claim with the same layers is caught. An honest driller pays 26 once and recovers the bond after a clean audit.
